```json
{"claims":[{"claim_text":"By 2020, the Republican bill will end the ACA’s expansion of Medicaid to close to 14 million individuals from working families that earn between $22,000 and $34,000 a year, an expansion paid for almost exclusively by federal funds for the 31 states that accepted the funding.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Nineteen Republican-governed states kept over 8 million individuals from receiving the Medicaid expansion.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The Republican plan would turn Medicaid’s guarantee of coverage to nearly 70 million individuals from an individual entitlement to a less generously funded federal “block grant” or “per capita” allotment.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Republicans claim the federal “block grant” or “per capita” allotment would provide “flexibility for the states”.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Such flexibility will allow states to reduce benefits and remove people from Medicaid.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The Medicare trust fund will be drained of income by ending the ACA’s surtax on the wealthy.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[2]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```
